title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Documented University of North Dakota ceremonies, gatherings, and campus practices with direct institutional sources.

cards.title: Mark UND’s February birthday
cards.subtitle: Annual Founders Day observance
cards.notes: Watch UND’s Founders Day announcements each February to see how the university marks its 1883 founding and recognizes campus service.
cards.short_summary: A February banquet tradition that began in 1904.
cards.evidence_claim: UND says its Founders Day tradition started in 1904 and annually aligns with the university’s February 27, 1883 founding date.
cards.access_notes: Event format and attendance details vary; consult the current Founders Day page.

cards.title: See cultures take the stage
cards.subtitle: UND International Organization’s annual celebration
cards.notes: Follow the International Organization’s event details for the annual dinner, cultural displays, and performances started by students in 1961.
cards.short_summary: A student-organized multicultural gathering with a 1961 origin.
cards.evidence_claim: UND states that Feast of Nations began in 1961, was organized by students in the International Organization, and is hosted annually.
cards.access_notes: Tickets are required for the event; review the current Feast of Nations information before attending.

cards.title: Join the Homecoming parade route
cards.subtitle: Annual UND fall tradition
cards.notes: Check the annual Homecoming schedule for parade, volunteer, alumni, and game-day events rather than assuming a repeating program.
cards.short_summary: A weeklong fall tradition first held at UND in 1916.
cards.evidence_claim: UND reports that its first Homecoming was held in 1916 and that the annual celebration has grown into a week of events.
cards.access_notes: Use the current UND Homecoming schedule for dates, locations, and participation details.

cards.title: Learn UND’s school song
cards.subtitle: University song tradition
cards.notes: Use UND’s published lyrics to recognize the school song at university occasions and athletic events; participate only where appropriate.
cards.short_summary: UND’s official school song pledges loyalty to North Dakota.
cards.evidence_claim: UND’s history page identifies “Stand Up and Cheer” as its school song and publishes its lyrics.
cards.access_notes: The official lyrics and a linked performance are available on UND’s history page.

cards.title: Spot the original prairie-rose colors
cards.subtitle: UND’s founding-color tradition
cards.notes: Look for historically themed green-and-pink displays and read the university’s account of why students chose the colors in 1889.
cards.short_summary: UND continues to recognize green and pink alongside today’s green and white.
cards.evidence_claim: UND says 25 students selected green and pink in 1889, and that the university continues to celebrate their special significance.
cards.access_notes: This is a historical color legacy, not a scheduled event; see UND’s history page for context.

cards.entity_name: RAIN Traditional Meal and Honor Ceremony
cards.title: Honor RAIN graduates through ceremony
cards.subtitle: College of Nursing & Professional Disciplines
cards.notes: Follow RAIN’s spring announcements for its graduate celebration, which includes a shared meal, Star Quilt presentations, honor songs, and a Friendship Dance.
cards.short_summary: A spring RAIN graduate celebration rooted in culture and community.
cards.evidence_claim: UND says the RAIN Program hosts a spring Traditional Meal and Honor Ceremony featuring a traditional meal, Star Quilt presentations, honor songs, and a Friendship Dance.
cards.access_notes: This program-specific ceremony is hosted each spring; consult RAIN for participation details.

cards.entity_name: College of Engineering & Mines Ring Ceremony
cards.title: Witness the engineer’s commitment
cards.subtitle: UND College of Engineering & Mines
cards.notes: Look for the college’s Ring Ceremony coverage to see graduating engineers and scientists mark their commitment to ethical professional practice.
cards.short_summary: A time-honored UND engineering milestone tied to professional responsibility.
cards.evidence_claim: UND describes its Ring Ceremony as a time-honored college event where students commit to ethical practice, service, and lifelong professionalism.
cards.access_notes: This ceremony is associated with College of Engineering & Mines students; check college announcements for invitations.

cards.title: Welcome new citizens on Constitution Day
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union observance
cards.notes: Check UND’s September Constitution Day program for the campus naturalization ceremony and related public events before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A recent annual campus observance on September 17.
cards.evidence_claim: UND reported that, over the past few years, holding a naturalization ceremony on campus on September 17 has become an annual tradition.
cards.source_title: UND to celebrate Constitution Day on Sept. 17
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current year’s Constitution Day program; the cited ceremony was listed at the Memorial Union.

cards.title: Follow UND football’s holiday giving tradition
cards.subtitle: UND Football community initiative
cards.notes: Read the annual Holiday Magic From Markus updates to understand how UND football players help prepare and deliver gifts for participating families.
cards.short_summary: A football-led holiday initiative that has continued for more than two decades.
cards.evidence_claim: UND reports that Holiday Magic From Markus has been a UND Football tradition for more than 20 years, with players shopping for, wrapping, and delivering gifts.
cards.source_title: STORY and VIDEO: The Magic endures
cards.access_notes: This is a football-program giving initiative; follow its current updates rather than expecting public participation.

cards.title: Look for Old Main’s oak in the procession
cards.subtitle: UND commencement ceremonial object
cards.notes: At a UND commencement, watch for the mace carried by a marshal and placed on stage as part of the academic procession.
cards.short_summary: A commencement mace made from oak from UND’s first building, Old Main.
cards.evidence_claim: UND states that its mace, made from oak from Old Main, is carried by a marshal during academic processions and placed on stage at commencement.
cards.access_notes: The mace appears as part of commencement ceremonial protocol; attend only through the event’s applicable invitation or ticket process.
